title: Road detours
notes: Keep one adult at each table; the youngest adult can record road names while children choose and replay. K-1 Problems 1-2 form the first route: three/four-step tree journeys, then four-step ring home trips. Use one ordered card for each actual road traversal; remove only adjacent opposite traversals of the same road and replay the rest. The original longer investigations remain as Problems 3-7 for a later visit or when ready. Grades 2-3 can return to two-ring order puzzles (P5-6); Grades 4-5 can separate unique reduction (P4) from zero-net-count obstructions (P5-6). The actual tile/mat/pawn procedure remains physically untested.

Problem 1: the three-step A-to-E trip is A-B-D-E. Every four-step B-home trip reduces to staying at B; every four-step A-to-D trip reduces to A-B-D. For example B-A-B-A-B disappears, while A-B-A-B-D leaves A-B-D. Problem 2: the possible reduced four-step ring home results are stay at A, A-B-C-D-A, and A-D-C-B-A. A nonempty reduced ring trip keeps one direction; the two circuits survive. The continuation key is renumbered Problems 3-7.
